preDevolution.heading: UK Unified Statutory Rating Framework (Pre-Devolution: 1990–2004)
preDevolution.statute: Local Government Finance Act 1988 (LGFA 1988 s.43, s.45, s.58)
preDevolution.overview: Prior to the Local Government Act 2003 reforms which took effect on 1 April 2005, England operated under the original unified Great Britain non-domestic rating framework enacted by Parliament in the LGFA 1988.
rules: Single Unified Multiplier: A single non-domestic multiplier (e.g. 34.8p in 1990/91) applied to all non-domestic hereditaments. No small business multiplier existed.
Zero Small Business Relief: Small Business Rate Relief (SBRR) did not exist. Every property, regardless of size, paid pure gross liability (Rateable Value × Single Multiplier).

Symmetrical 5-Year Transitional Phasing: Revaluations under LGFA 1988 s.58 featured upward caps (+15%/+20%) funded by downward reduction caps that delayed bill reductions for falling-value properties, indexed to annual RPI.

Pre-2008 Empty Property Rules: Empty commercial premises received 3 months 100% exemption, then paid 50% rates indefinitely; industrial hereditaments enjoyed 100% permanent exemption until the Rating (Empty Properties) Act 2007 imposed 100% empty liability on 1 April 2008.

preDevolution.heading: UK Unified Statutory Rating Framework (Pre-Devolution: 1990–1999/2004)
preDevolution.statute: Local Government Finance Act 1988 (Secretary of State for Wales orders)
preDevolution.overview: Prior to the transfer of rating order powers to the National Assembly for Wales under the Government of Wales Act 1998 and the later introduction of devolved Welsh SBRR in 2005, Wales operated under common UK rating regulations.
rules: Unified National Multiplier: Wales shared a single non-domestic multiplier set nationally (e.g. 36.8p in 1990/91, 39.0p in 1995/96) with no small business differentiation.
Zero Small Business Relief: Pre-devolution Welsh rating lists provided 0% small business relief; full rates were payable on all commercial properties.
Symmetrical 5-Year Transitional Phasing: LGFA 1988 s.58 applied across Wales, featuring symmetrical upward protection caps funded by downward phasing reduction caps, indexed to RPI.
Pre-2008 Empty Rates: Empty commercial hereditaments received 3 months 100% exemption, then paid 50% rates indefinitely until empty rate parity was introduced in 2008.

preDevolution.heading: UK Unified Statutory Rating Framework (Pre-Devolution: 1990–1999/2008)
preDevolution.overview: Prior to devolution under the Scotland Act 1998 and the subsequent creation of the Small Business Bonus Scheme (SBBS) on 1 April 2008, non-domestic rates in Scotland were administered under the UK Scottish Office framework.
rules: Single Scottish Poundage: A single uniform poundage rate (e.g. 52.5p in 1990/91, 43.2p in 1995/96) was set by the Secretary of State for Scotland, applied uniformly across all commercial properties.
Pre-SBBS Era: No universal small business relief existed until the pilot Small Business Rate Relief Scheme (SBRRS) in 2003, which was later replaced by SBBS in 2008.
Symmetrical Transitional Phasing: Scottish revaluations featured symmetrical transitional phasing schemes capping annual poundage shifts with upward limits and downward delay caps.
Pre-2008 Empty Rating: 3 months initial empty property exemption followed by 50% indefinite rating.
